name: System Ration
description: A sealed tray the System hands out to regressors. It tastes like nothing, which is the point: nothing is what the old world has left. Restores 45 hunger. Season 2.

name: Rift Bandage
description: Cloth that closes the wound and argues with the scar afterwards. Restores 220 HP when used. Season 2.

name: Rift Fragment
description: A shard of the space between worlds, still warm. Gate work and tower crafting will want it. Season 2.

name: Survival Scrap
description: Straps, buckles, wire and one hinge you will never find a use for. The shelter builds its tools out of this. Season 2.

name: Survivor's Boots
description: Soles worn thin by floors that tried to keep you. They have learned the shape of every stair in the tower and refuse to stop on one. Season 2.

name: Probability Ring
description: A band that quietly disagrees with the odds. Wear it and the coin lands on its edge a little more often than it should. Season 2.

name: Taleweaver's Quill
description: It writes in the margin of the fight. Every spell you cast is a sentence it finishes for you, a half-beat before you thought of it. Season 2.

name: Dokkaebi Mask
description: The face the scenarios wear when they want to be watched. Put it on and the tower hesitates, just for a moment, unsure who is running whom. Season 2.

name: Regressor's Coat
description: Cut from the long walk back to the start. It has been through the end of the world already and came out the other side still buttoned. Season 2.

name: Constellation Crown
description: A circle of small lights that answers to no sky. Wear it and the things above the tower notice you back. Season 2.

name: Starlight Aegis
description: A shield made of the light a star sends out before it dies. It has already outlived one apocalypse and intends to outlive yours. Season 2.

name: Fourth Wall Mantle
description: The wall itself, worn as a coat. Blows land on the story of you instead of on you, and the story is harder to kill. Season 2.

name: Star Stream Ration
description: A meal broadcast from somewhere kinder. It tastes like the memory of food, which is enough to keep a regressor moving. Restores 80 hunger. Season 2.

name: Fourth Wall Tea
description: Steeped from leaves that grew on the quiet side of the wall. It settles the part of you that keeps reading ahead. Restores 50 hunger. Season 2.

name: Dokkaebi Firewater
description: It burns going down and keeps burning in the arm. For three turns the System counts your strength a little higher than it is. Season 2.

name: Probability Tonic
description: A mouthful of loaded dice. For the next three hits the odds lean your way and the damage leans with them. Season 2.

name: Ironbulwark Draught
description: It turns the skin into a rumor of iron. Three blows land on the rumor instead of on you. Season 2.

name: Scenario Ward
description: A folded clause of protection. It absorbs the next 600 damage the scenario tries to write onto you. Season 2.

name: Constellation Elixir
description: Distilled attention from a constellation that wants you alive. It closes wounds the way a reader closes a gap in the plot. Restores 900 HP. Season 2.

name: Regression Potion
description: It rewinds the body to an earlier, less broken draft. Restores 2500 HP. The System does not ask which version of you it is keeping. Season 2.

name: Rift Ambrosia
description: The space between worlds, bottled and sweetened. It refills every spent art in a single swallow. Restores all MP. Season 2.

name: Phoenix Tear
description: One drop kept from a bird that refuses to end. The next killing blow lands, and then quietly decides it did not. Season 2.

name: Constellation Sigil
description: A mark a constellation leaves when it sponsors a climb. Gate work and the deep crafting benches ask for it by name. Season 2.

name: Scenario Ink
description: The black the System writes its rules in. Still wet, still binding. Used to temper tower gear and to sign contracts you should read twice. Season 2.

name: Tower Key Fragment
description: A piece of the thing that opens floors that are not on the stair. Enough of them and a locked wing remembers it was meant to be climbed. Season 2.
